items.title: CMS Energy plans to sell renewable assets to focus on regulated utilities
items.summary: The Jackson, Michigan-based company said the move would simplify its corporate structure, net about $500 million and set it up to generate nearly all of its earnings from its regulated utilities after 2027.

items.title: China’s solar market heads for first annual contraction since 2019
items.summary: The China Photovoltaic Industry Association says domestic installations are returning to more sustainable levels but expects both China’s market and global PV additions to shrink in 2026. The post China’s solar market heads for first annual contraction since 2019 appeared first on pv magazine Global .

items.title: CAB® Solar highlights solar cable hanger solutions for agricultural projects
items.summary: At The smarter E 2026 in Munich, the company demonstrated its ModulAir® free-air cable hangers for solar projects, as well as its latest 3D locking hangers, which are designed to secure electric cables when used in locations with livestock. items.title: Georgia Power completes construction of 198MWh BESS next to Moody Air Force Base
items.summary: Utility Georgia Power has completed construction of the 49.5MW/198MWh Moody Battery Facility, located outside of Valdosta, Georgia, US.

items.title: US bans foreign-produced solar inverters
items.summary: In the United States, the Federal Communications Commission Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau has added foreign-produced power inverters to its Covered List, executing an immediate ban on equipment authorizations for unapproved foreign models over national security and hacking concerns. items.title: Serbia adds 61 MW of solar in H1
items.summary: After the first six months of the year, Serbia’s solar capacity reached around 379 MW. While the country’s green energy market has been impacted by delays in permitting and grid connection processes, its prosumer market continues to grow. The post Serbia adds 61 MW of solar in H1 appeared first on pv magazine Global .

items.title: ‘Tremendously important market for storage’: US BESS integrator FlexGen on its start of European operations
items.summary: ESN Premium speaks with Jason Abiecunas and Mike Wallace of FlexGen, one of a growing number of US BESS companies establishing operations in Europe.

items.title: RWE building 470MWh BESS in Germany; Kallista enlists Envision for 386MWh in France
items.summary: RWE has launched construction on a 236MW/470MWh BESS in Germany, while IPP Kallista has done the same on a 193MW/386MWh system in France, supplied by Envision Energy.

items.title: Why consumers are choosing solar over fossil fuels
items.summary: People across the world have woken up to the fact that renewable energy is a source of local economic stability and energy security, particularly when it’s on their roofs, with a recent global survey finding two in three people now support renewable energy and storage investment. items.title: Financing secured for Timor-Leste’s first solar-storage project
items.summary: The Asian Development Bank, World Bank and investors from Canada and Japan have partnered on a $85.7 million financing package for Timor-Leste’s first independent power project. The post Financing secured for Timor-Leste’s first solar-storage project appeared first on pv magazine Global .

items.title: Bhutan tenders solar systems for three schools
items.summary: A tender is open in Bhutan for three rooftop solar systems to serve three separate schools. The deadline for applications is August 24. The post Bhutan tenders solar systems for three schools appeared first on pv magazine Global .

items.title: German battery manufacturer files for self-administered insolvency
items.summary: German battery manufacturer Varta has filed for self-administered insolvency, with the proceedings covering its solar-storage and energy management business. The post German battery manufacturer files for self-administered insolvency appeared first on pv magazine Global .

items.title: Neoen Australia begins construction on 907MWh grid-forming BESS in South Australia
items.summary: Neoen Australia has commenced construction of a 227MW/907MWh grid-forming battery storage system in South Australia.

items.title: NEM battery price spreads fall 85% in a year as Australia’s grid-scale BESS fleet passes 9,000MW
items.summary: NEM-wide battery price spreads fell 85% in a single year to average AU$51/MWh (US$35/MWh) in Q2 2026, according to AEMO.

items.title: Quinbrook’s Supernode BESS becomes the largest in operation across Australia’s NEM
items.summary: Quinbrook has completed construction and commenced commercial operations at Stage 2 of its Supernode BESS in Australia.

items.title: Behind the New York data center pause is legislation that could impact existing facilities
items.summary: Legislation that’s been put on the back burner while the moratorium is in effect would require large data centers to procure at least a third of their electricity from renewable sources by 2030 and might impact those with water-intensive cooling, analyses show.

items.title: Community solar can bridge California’s energy affordability gap
items.summary: Regulatory complexities are thwarting innovation and keeping electricity bills for the majority of Californians far too high, writes Ardi Arian, CEO of Renewable America.

items.title: PJM board proposes backstop capacity auction, data center curtailment plans
items.summary: FERC’s response to the proposals will likely “influence utility capital investment, data center development timelines and the allocation of reliability risks and costs,” ClearView Energy Partners said.

items.title: BNEF chip-based model pegs US data center demand at 207 GW by 2033
items.summary: A base model anticipates U.S. data center demand of about 118 GW by 2030. As potential demand and proposed data center size both grow, so does the complexity in forecasting, analysts said.

items.title: CenterPoint says 14 GW likely eligible for Texas’ ‘Batch Zero’ large-load interconnection
items.summary: The utility expects 50% load growth by the end of 2029, largely driven by data centers navigating Texas’ new large-load interconnection process, company officials said Tuesday.

items.title: Slovakian battery and BESS manufacturer InoBat eyes SPAC merger for Nasdaq listing
items.summary: European battery manufacturer and energy storage system integrator InoBat plans to get a Nasdaq listing through a business combination with a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC).

items.title: Inside the container: looking at CATL’s sodium-ion Tener’s specs
items.summary: In this deep-dive, we go through and analyse all of the technical features and claims of CATL's new sodium-ion grid-scale BESS product, including its 'millisecond-level self-healing'.

items.title: VIDEO: How Envision Energy is positioning itself as a system-level energy infrastructure provider
items.summary: We caught up with Kevin Huang, Senior Vice President and President of Energy Storage Product Line at Envision Energy at Smarter E in Munich for a video interview on the company's energy storage strategy and the growing role of AI data centres in power demand.

items.title: Zenobē buys German BESS developer SDP Energie, inheriting 1.75GW transmission-level pipeline
items.summary: UK-based BESS and EV charging firm Zenobē has entered the German market with the acquisition of Bavaria-headquartered BESS developer SDP Energie.

items.title: Minister of Energy leads ceremony to commission Malawi’s first grid-scale standalone BESS
items.summary: Malawi’s energy minister was on hand last week as the southeast African country inaugurated its first large-scale standalone battery energy storage system (BESS).

items.title: Malaysia launches tender for 2.5GW of solar PV with co-located battery storage
items.summary: The government of Malaysia has unveiled the next round of its Large-scale solar (LSS) program tender seeking 2.5GW of solar PV co-located with 1.25GW of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity.

items.title: Hanoi Power Corporation inaugurates the first 100MWh battery storage portfolio in Vietnamese capital
items.summary: Hanoi Power Corporation (EVNHANOI) has begun pilot operation of five battery energy storage systems at substations in Hanoi, Vietnam.

items.title: States cannot be granted filing rights under Section 205 of the Federal Power Act
items.summary: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission should reject a proposal that states share “filing rights” with the PJM Interconnection and its transmission owners, former FERC Chairman Joseph Kelliher writes.

items.title: Vehicle-to-grid added to Massachusetts utilities’ ConnectedSolutions demand response VPP
items.summary: Eversource and National Grid will enable customers in Massachusetts to enrol vehicle-to-grid (V2G) -capable EVs in their demand side flexibility programme.

items.title: Energy storage generates nearly 20% of CATL’s revenues in first half of 2026
items.summary: CATL’s energy storage division represented 19.23% of the Chinese battery manufacturer’s total revenue in the first half of 2026.

items.title: Ark Energy locks in AU$1.3 billion for 2.2GWh solar-plus-storage site in New South Wales, Australia
items.summary: Two Australian solar-plus-storage projects advance: Ark Energy secures AU$1.3 billion for 2.2GWh Richmond Valley project; Quinbrook submits 250MWp Queensland site.

items.title: Poland: R.Power enlists EPCs for 2.2GWh of BESS, EDF and Eurus, Eiffel and Ergy co-invest in projects
items.summary: It's been a busy week for the large-scale energy storage market in Poland, with projects moved to construction and delivery by EDF Power Solutions & Eurus Energy Europe, Eiffel Investment Group & Ergy, R.Power Renewables, and EDP.
